newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp debt players cautious ahead of jobs data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp debt players cautious ahead of jobs data.

text.p: Several corporate debt deals are slated to come to market on Thursday but higher interest rates and fears of further Federal Reserve tightening has forced others to shelve their offerings, dealers said.
"Employment data and fears that rates may be nudged up again has kept buyers on the sidelines and caused others to run for cover," said one syndicate source.
Players are keeping a close watch on Friday's U.S. nonfarm payrolls data for further clues on the strength of the U.S. economy.
"New (corporate debt) issues are being held hostage by tomorrow's numbers," said another syndicate source.
In a Reuter poll, U.S. economists predict March unemployment will dip slightly to 5.2 percent and expect an increase of 182,000 in nonfarm payrolls, versus an increase of 339,000 in February.
Meanwhile, in the face of rising interest rates several deals have been postponed, dealers said.
On Thursday, lead underwriter BancAmerica Securities said it postponed a $150 million junk bond deal for Station Casinos until May.
"Corporate spreads are out and stocks are off substantially from their highs...junk bonds have really taken it on the chin with several deals geting postponed," a syndicate source said.
And Comcast Corp unit Comcast Cellular Holdings' debt offering was postponed as well, according to market sources.
Sources speculated the current deterioration in high-yield prices prompted the move.
"That's going to trickle up in quality," the syndicate source added. "It's going to put pressure on that whole area...BB crossover credits will be impacted."
Meanwhile, among investment-grade deals expected to come to market on Thursday is GTE Corp's $500 million A3/A-minus 12-year note deal via Salomon Brothers, dealers said.
Also, Amgen Inc is slated to bring its 100-year bond via joint managers Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch, sources said.
Bank United is also expected to tap the market with a two-part $220 million debt offering of subordinated notes via Smith Barney, sources added.
It is expected to consist of $100 million in seven-year notes and $120 million in 10-year notes, they said.

In the junk sector, Bellwether Exploration is expected to come to market later today with $100 million in B1/B-minus rated 10-year senior notes via JP Morgan Securities. Price talk on the issue is seen between 350 and 375 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, sources said.
Also, Triton Energy Corp is set to bring a $400 million two-part Ba2/BB rated senior note debt offering via Bear Stearns and Salomon Brothers, sources said.
The first tranche consist of $200 million in five-year notes and $200 million in 30-year notes, putable in ten years, sources added.
Despite the tough issuing environment several issuers may still venture into the primary arena for fear that financing rates may go even higher, dealers said.
On Friday, all eyes are expected to focus on the Labor Department's release of the March jobs report and any forthcoming Fed policy implications that can be drawn from it.

"The market doesn't have that general euphoric feeling of a month ago," said another syndicate source. "We were trading at such tight levels for so long it had to crack...it's kind of tough right now," he added.
In the government market, the bencmark U.S. 30-year bond was trading off 2/32 at 94-12/32 to yield 7.08 percent.
(( --Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675 ))
